clue.text: Suit and tie

definitions.meaning: to suit is to go well with, to be a good pairing for
a tie is a sporting contest or fixture between two sides

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a colour that suits another goes with it, and a cup tie is a fixture between teams.

clue.text: An unwanted increase: 500 to 1500, say?

definitions.meaning: the thickening waistline that tends to arrive with the forties and fifties
the medieval period stretched across roughly a thousand years, read as the era's extent

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as 'the Middle Ages' span', the medieval era stretching from about AD 500 to 1500.
explanation.definitionFit: Weight gained round the waist in later life is an unwelcome increase, and the medieval era spread over those centuries.

clue.text: When one line fails, fully ready to switch electrical unit

indicators.note: to switch here means to turn round, so the remaining letters are read in reverse order
one line failing means one L drops out of the phrase for completely prepared

parts.note: all set means fully ready

explanation.surface: An electrician's warning: lose one supply line and the fully primed system will switch over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When one line fails' takes one L from ALLSET, leaving ALSET, and 'to switch' turns ALSET round. A tesla is strictly a magnetic unit, a loose fit for 'electrical'.
explanation.definitionFit: The tesla is the SI unit of magnetic flux density, named after the inventor Nikola Tesla.

clue.text: Silent film actor playing killer at sea

parts.note: Harpo Marx never spoke on screen, playing his role in silence
on, as in on stage, means playing or performing

explanation.surface: A silent-screen star cast as a murderer aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silent film actor' points to Harpo Marx, the Marx brother who never spoke on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A harpoon is the barbed spear used to kill whales, so a killer at sea.

clue.text: Creole food post taken by a remarkable pork-pie producer?

parts.note: a jamb is an upright post at the side of a door or window

indicators.note: remarkable read as able to be remarked, that is, spoken, so the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: porky pies is Cockney rhyming slang for lies, so their producer is someone who tells them

explanation.surface: A Creole dish is the post won by a brilliant pork-pie maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pork-pie' is British rhyming slang (porky pies = lies). A LIAR said aloud gives the ALAYA ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Jambalaya is the spicy Louisiana rice dish of Creole and Cajun cooking.

clue.text: Yank gets appropriate neighbours to welcome queen

indicators.note: to welcome is to take someone in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: J and K are neighbours in the alphabet, and in a pack of cards they flank the queen, which makes them fitting neighbours here
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the queen

explanation.surface: An American finds the right people next door to receive the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' because in a suit of cards the jack and king sit either side of the queen. 'Yank' looks like a noun for an American but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To yank something is to pull it suddenly, the same as a sharp tug.

clue.text: American mother, fed up with nonsense, dismissed husband — he's a bore

indicators.note: being fed means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Mom is the American word for mother

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: rot means nonsense
a batter who is dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: An American woman, sick of rubbish, throws out her spouse, who bores her stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed up' looks like 'tired of', but the phrase splits: 'up' turns the nonsense word round and 'fed' stuffs it inside the American mother. In cricket, a batter who is dismissed is out.
explanation.definitionFit: A motormouth talks incessantly, which makes him a tiresome bore to listeners.

clue.text: In a poll, firm preference initially expressed for fizzy drink

indicators.note: In places the firm and the initial inside the other pieces

parts.note: to poll a tree is to lop or cut off its top
CO, company, is the usual abbreviation for a firm

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: In an opinion poll, the drink most people prefer turns out to be a sparkling one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poll' looks like a survey, but here it is the verb meaning cut the top off a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcopop is a sweet, fizzy, ready-mixed alcoholic drink sold in bottles.

clue.text: Note included in a gratuity covering wine and starters

indicators.note: being included in something means going inside it

parts.note: a tip is a gratuity
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine, and in this down entry it sits under the first part, which covers it

explanation.surface: A small extra added to the tip to pay for the wine with the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down entry the first part sits above, or 'covering', the wine. Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont, Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasti are Italian appetisers served before the main meal, so starters.

clue.text: One making a phenomenal contribution to Cook's tour down under

definitions.text: One making a phenomenal contribution to Cook's tour down under

parts.words: One making a phenomenal contribution to Cook's tour down under
parts.note: Captain Cook's southern voyage would have shown the southern lights, a natural phenomenon of the far south

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook's tour' suggests a package holiday, but this is Captain Cook sailing the southern oceans, where he saw the southern lights.
explanation.definitionFit: The southern lights are a natural light display seen in far southern skies, a phenomenon of the Antipodes.

clue.text: Soldier devastated trees in blast

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: drat and blast are both mild curses

indicators.note: devastated means wrecked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Explosions flattened the woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blast' looks like an explosion, matching 'devastated', but it is the mild curse. 'devastated' rearranges the trees, and 'in' puts them inside the curse after its D.
explanation.definitionFit: The Desert Rats were the British 7th Armoured Division in North Africa, so one is a soldier.

clue.text: Provide entertainment and grub without support

indicators.note: without means the second piece is taken away

parts.note: a caterpillar is a grub, the larva of a butterfly or moth
a pillar is a support

explanation.surface: Laying on a show and food with no backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' looks like food, set beside 'entertainment', but it is the insect larva.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to supply what is needed, including food or amusement, for guests.

clue.text: Trick metal leg

parts.note: lead is a heavy metal
the leg side in cricket is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A con involving a leaden limb.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone on is to deceive them, which is to trick them.

clue.text: A part played by the Cartoonists' Foundation?

indicators.note: played means acted out in a different way, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: A role taken on by the founding body of cartoonists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' rearranges A PART into ARTPA.
explanation.definitionFit: Art paper is coated paper that drawings are made on, the base for cartoonists' work.

clue.text: Pathetic device distinctively identified in a German explosive

parts.note: limp means feeble or pathetic

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: eine is German for a
TM, trademark, is a device that marks out goods distinctively

explanation.surface: A feeble gadget, clearly marked, inside a German bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'device distinctively identified' describes a trade mark, TM, a mark that identifies goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A limpet mine is an explosive device that clings magnetically to a ship's hull.

clue.text: Slowish vote for yes … ?

definitions.meaning: a musical direction for a tempo a little slower than walking pace
a vote for yes is a vote with the ayes and against the noes

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: voting for yes means being, as the split answer says, AND ANTI NO. The ellipsis invites the solver to continue the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Andantino is a musical tempo marking, usually a little faster than andante, so moderately slow.

clue.text: Huge number upset about remote cheese-shop supplier

indicators.note: about means going around something else
in a down clue, upset means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a myriad is a huge number
far means distant or remote

explanation.surface: A vast crowd, angry about something far off, supplies a cheesemonger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns MYRIAD into DAIRYM, which goes 'about' FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairy farm produces the milk from which cheese is made, supplying the cheesemonger.

clue.text: Italian food and Spanish food in rotation

indicators.note: rotating moves letters round from one end to the other

parts.note: tapas are Spanish snacks

explanation.surface: Restaurants serving Italian and Spanish dishes on alternating nights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in rotation' moves TA from the front of TAPAS to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is the staple Italian dough food, spaghetti and the like.

clue.text: Writer rejecting dress material

indicators.note: rejecting means turning back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: toile is a fine fabric used for dresses and dress patterns

explanation.surface: An author turning down a fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' turns TOILE back to front. George Eliot and T S Eliot are both writers.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot and T S Eliot are both famous writers in English.

clue.text: Legend delivered in two halves for the kids?

definitions.text: Legend delivered in two halves for the kids?

parts.words: Legend delivered in two halves for the kids?
parts.note: split the word legend in two to get leg end, the foot, which children call by a pet name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Legend' split into 'leg end' gives the foot, and 'for the kids' asks for the nursery word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tootsie is a child's word for a foot, the lowest end of the leg.

clue.text: One catching fish to fill baked dishes in this area of industry

indicators.note: to fill means going inside something else

parts.note: pies are baked dishes
an otter is an animal that hunts fish

explanation.surface: A fisherman stuffing pies in an industrial district.
explanation.walkthrough: The Potteries is the Stoke-on-Trent area of England, famous for making ceramics.
explanation.definitionFit: The Potteries is the pottery-making district of Staffordshire, an industrial region of England.

clue.text: Sign one's being talked about outside it?

definitions.text: Sign one's being talked about outside it?

parts.words: Sign one's being talked about outside it?
parts.note: the old saying is that burning ears show people are gossiping about you out of range

explanation.walkthrough: Folk belief says your ears burn when people talk about you: that would be 'ears hot', and the talk happens beyond your hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Earshot is the range of hearing, so gossip outside it is out of hearing distance.

clue.text: Keep working opening that the Pilgrims left

parts.note: to ply a trade is to keep working at it
a mouth is an opening

explanation.surface: Keep at it through the gap the Pilgrims went through.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pilgrim Fathers sailed from Plymouth, in Devon, on the Mayflower in 1620.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pilgrim Fathers sailed for America from the Devon port on the Mayflower in 1620.

clue.text: One supplying households gets more obscene on the phone

indicators.note: on the phone means spoken and heard, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: grosser means more vulgar or obscene

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper turns crude when he picks up the phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the phone' signals that the word is given by its sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A grocer sells food and household goods, so supplies households.

clue.text: Way down South, author's lost it after chapter's written

indicators.note: after means this piece comes behind the chapter letter

parts.note: C is an abbreviation for chapter, here written down first

indicators.note: the writer losing it means the letter for South drops out of his name

parts.note: Nevil Shute was an English novelist, author of A Town Like Alice

explanation.surface: Down south, a writer has lost the plot after finishing his chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way down South' reads as a place, but 'Way down' is the definition. The novelist Nevil Shute loses his S, and the rest follows C for chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: A chute is a sloping channel things slide down, so a way down.

clue.text: Well filled-out with one in short order

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: fat means plump or well filled-out
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Being nicely plump, with someone in, quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short order' reads as 'quickly', but 'short order' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiat is a brief, authoritative command or decree.

clue.text: 17's riding in luggage van, somehow

indicators.note: riding in means sitting inside, so the word is concealed inside these words

explanation.surface: An author's luggage is going in a van, by some means.
explanation.walkthrough: George Eliot's real name was Mary Ann Evans, so EVANS is 17's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot was the pen name of Mary Ann Evans, so this is her real surname.

clue.text: Awful hubris permeates sick non sequitur

indicators.note: permeating means getting inside

parts.note: ill means sick

indicators.note: awful means terrible, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Terrible arrogance spreads through an unwell person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges HUBRIS to RISHBU, which 'permeates' ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish bull is a ludicrous, self-contradictory statement, a nonsensical logical leap.

clue.text: The very best garden bananas viewed over street

indicators.note: viewed over means looked at from the other side, so read backwards

parts.note: Eden is the garden in Genesis
bananas means crazy or mad

explanation.surface: Bananas in the garden, seen across the road, are top quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewed over' reverses EDEN + MAD to give DAMNEDE, then ST is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To do one's damnedest is to do one's utmost, the very best one can.

clue.text: Lock physical pressure's broken top off

indicators.note: with its top broken off, the first letter goes

parts.note: stress is physical pressure

explanation.surface: A lock snaps under physical strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' looks like a fastening, but it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock of hair.
